points.text: 'Theoretical argument for inevitability' corresponds only to definitions and asserted inequalities.
Efficiency superiority claim unsupported; no measured cost.
'Informing safety alignment' claim has no alignment experiment.
Definitions split across appendix; cross-reference, caption and model-count inconsistencies.
JOCR description in main text omits question-rewriting step revealed in appendix.
No limitations section; ethics and reproducibility statements do not describe this paper.
No defense-side experiment (OCR guard, safety fine-tuning) despite alignment claims.
Latent analysis on one 7B open model applied to closed models.
Attack success judged by one LLM judge without manual harm assessment.
Premise that pretraining contains perturbed text-in-image samples unevidenced.
Dual-use and vendor disclosure not discussed; ethics statement mismatched.
Intent and refusal probe token positions swapped relative to stated premise.
Intent probe is self-similarity, high by construction; no benign/random controls.
Refusal probe dimensions inconsistent, undescribed logit lens, token list and controls missing.
Trade-off not linked per-sample to ASR; refusal trend fails to explain ASR downturn.
Probes run on different models than ASR curves.
Fig. 4 decay contrast is an artifact of independent axis scaling.
PCA argument is 2-D projection without distances; conflicts with other trends.
Pre-training vs alignment attribution untested; single aligned model used.
No theorem derived; inevitability argument is assumptions only.
SI-attack and JOOD excluded from JOCR comparison without adaptation.
'Over 10% higher than baselines' false per cell; one cell lower.
Single GPT-4o judge, also a target; no human validation or threshold.
Undisclosed rewriting step not controlled in comparisons.
Single run per cell; no CIs; small differences indistinguishable.
Universality claim lacks zero-perturbation baselines; some effects within noise.
Ablations on headline benchmark; configuration selection unstated; small differences over-read.
Minor: Eq. 2 wording, equation references, layer range, table row and value inconsistencies.
'First from feature perspective' inaccurate given HiddenDetect, Internal Activation Revision.
Citation errors: CS-DJ misattributed, GPT-4.1 to GPT-4 report, unrelated Liu et al.
JOCR is FigStep plus randomized typography; thin delta, much gain from generic shuffling.
SI-attack, JOOD and Visual Contextual Attack not compared.
Related work only in appendix and omits VLM hidden-state analysis/defense line.
Trade-off partly definitional; ASR downturn unexplained; no sample-level link.
Latent probes use swapped positions.
Intent probe is self-similarity.
Refusal probe dimensions inconsistent.
'First' claim not supported.
'Theoretical argument for inevitability' overclaimed.
Efficiency superiority claimed without cost measurement.
'Over 10%' ASR gain holds in only 4 of 12 cells.
No confidence intervals.
Pre-training/alignment attribution untested.
SI-attack and JOOD excluded from comparison.
Single judge that is also a target; ASR threshold unspecified.
JOCR rewriting step uncontrolled.
Universality without zero-perturbation baselines; effects within noise.
Ethics statement mismatched; no dual-use discussion.
Duplicate bibliography entries, missing CS-DJ, wrong GPT-4.1 citation.
Presentation slips: Fig. 5 layers, model count, Table 8 rows and values.
Pretrain-alignment asymmetry hypothesis not new (mismatched generalization, Wei et al.).
Weak-OOD phenomenon already observed in prior work such as JOOD.
JOCR lacks principled weak-OOD procedure; ad hoc tweaks on FigStep without intent guarantee.
Typos at L81 and L385.
Alternative explanation: generic non-robustness to low-level perturbations, not semantic OOD.
Weak-OOD notion close to established robustness ideas; novelty unclear.
Unclear whether robustness training on perturbations would fix the issue.
Why the phenomenon happens in practice is unclear; needs interpretation.
Averaging layer-wise similarities ignores layer heterogeneity.
No ablation of perturbation settings and their effect on intent and refusal.
Theory heuristic; latent interpretation relies on debated assumptions; evidence correlational.
Heavy reliance on shuffle perturbations to define OOD magnitude limits generalization.
GPT-4o judge may introduce bias.
JOCR builds on known typography idea plus random perturbations; limited methodological novelty.
Defenses not explored.

P.summary: Theoretical inevitability claim unsupported; no theorem.
JOCR rewriting step undisclosed and uncontrolled.
Missing limitations; mismatched ethics statement; no dual-use discussion.
Latent analysis models differ from attacked models.
Trade-off not shown to explain ASR curve.
Ablation protocol and configuration selection unclear.

Q.summary: JOCR ad hoc with limited novelty over typographic attacks.
Weak-OOD novelty vs robustness literature unclear.
